correctness.rationale: A relatively free algebra in the variety generated by a finite algebra is realized by the algebra of term functions on \(L^n\) generated by coordinate projections. Writing \(x_i=a_ie+b_if\), every commutator is \(f\)-valued and linear in \(b\); the basic coefficient vectors are \(s_{ij}(a)=a_i e_j-a_j e_i\). Bracketing an \(f\)-valued term with \(x_r\) multiplies its coefficient by \(-a_r\), so the derived ideal contains every polynomial-function multiple of every \(s_{ij}\). Since over \(\mathbb F_q\) every scalar function on \(k^n\) is represented by a polynomial, coefficients can be localized pointwise. For each nonzero \(a\), the vectors \(s_{ij}(a)\) span \(a^\perp\), while all vanish at the origin; conversely all brackets stay in this module. This proves the intrinsic description. The generator span has dimension \(n\) and intersects the derived ideal trivially, yielding the formula. The actual verifier independently closes term functions under brackets for small prime-field cases, and a separate reimplementation reproduced dimensions 5, 17, and 10 for \((q,n)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2)\).

value.rationale: The two-dimensional affine Lie algebra is the smallest nonabelian Lie algebra and appears as the base case of a recent finite-field growth construction. Replacing a known exponential rate by an exact formula at every free rank, together with a concrete intrinsic description of the derived ideal, is a natural structural refinement likely to be reusable in finite-field PI and locally finite variety questions.

final_claim: For the two-dimensional nonabelian Lie algebra \(L=ke\oplus kf\) over \(k=\mathbb F_q\) with \([e,f]=f\), the rank-\(n\) relatively free algebra in \(\operatorname{var}_k L\) has \[\dim_kF_n=n+(n-1)(q^n-1).\] In the term-function model its derived ideal is exactly the space of vector-valued coefficient functions \(F:k^n\to k^n\) satisfying \(F(0)=0\) and \(a\cdot F(a)=0\) for every \(a\), so \(\dim_k[F_n,F_n]=(n-1)(q^n-1)\).
limitations: The field is finite and the Lie algebra is exactly the two-dimensional affine Lie algebra.
The proof uses the fact that every function on \(\mathbb F_q^n\) is polynomial; no infinite-field analogue is claimed.
Higher-dimensional semidirect-product examples from the motivating growth paper are not solved.
